note: crops and livestock products: graded commodities (grain, oilseeds, feed); the same product from another region substitutes within days
coal and lignite; traded on quality specs
crude oil and gas; fungible within specs
sand, gravel, stone; local but interchangeable between sources
food, beverages, tobacco: mostly standard products with many suppliers (Barrot & Sauvagnat: no measurable propagation for non-specific inputs)
textiles, apparel, leather: specific to orders (Rauch differentiated)
refined petroleum products: fully fungible (diesel, gasoline, naphtha to spec); the substitution is limited by logistics, not by the product
basic chemicals, fertilisers, primary plastics: reference-priced commodities (Rauch); specialised chemicals are a minority of the sector's flows
rubber and plastic products: parts made to specification
cement, clinker, glass, building materials: standardised
basic iron and steel: graded semi-finished products (slabs, coils, rebar)
fabricated metal products: made to drawing
motor vehicles and parts (Boehm et al. 2019: sigma about 0.2 across sources)
electricity, gas, steam: fungible on the grid (the model has no grid; pooling stands in for it)
water supply, waste: local utilities, interchangeable sources
